newsitem.title: USA: Mobile Telecom reaches 1.3 mln units in 96.
newsitem.headline: Mobile Telecom reaches 1.3 mln units in 96.

text.p: Mobile Telecommunication Technologies Corp said it had 1,307,400 worldwide paging and messaging units in service at the end of 1996, an increase of 25.6 percent from 1995.
There were 1,083,200 domestic one-way units, 29,800 two-way units and 194,400 proportionate international units in service, the company said.

Mtel said its one-way paging business posted revenues of $78.4 million in the fourth quarter, a 17.5 percent increase over the same period in 1995. One-way operating cash flow was $25.8 million, representing a 33.0 percent operating cash flow margin and a 35 percent increase over fourth quarter 1995 results.

The company said its fourth-quarter consolidated revenue was $89.7 million compared with $74.1 million last year. Operating cash flow was $2.5 million in the fourth quarter compared with negative $24 million the same quarter of 1995.
The company also said its fourth-quarter results included a $38.8 million writedown, a majority of which related to international efforts in Europe and Asia.
"These adjustments allow us to eliminate the previously capitalized costs for proposed projects which we did not complete," said John Palmer, Mtel's chairman.

"You can't expect success in every development effort," Palmer said. "But the recently completed sale of a 20 percent equity interest in Mtel Latin America for $35 million, rendering an implied value of $175 million, demonstrates that our international efforts have brought real value to our shareholders."
Robert Kaiser, Mtel's chief financial officer, said he did not foresee any further adjustment in the "foreseeable future."
Including the writedown, Mtel reported a fourth-quarter loss of $82.0 million, or $1.57 per share, compared with a net loss of $40.4 million or $0.79 per share, last year.
